title: HTTPS in 60 seconds
caption: HTTPS in 60 seconds: what the padlock actually means, and how two strangers agree on a secret in public. #https #security #webdev

scenes.title: HTTPS
scenes.say: Anyone on your café Wi-Fi could read your traffic. Unless there's an S.
Between you and a website sits café wifi, your provider, and every router on the way. Plain HTTP is readable by all of them.
HTTPS wraps it in TLS, which adds three things.

items.title: Encryption
items.text: nobody in between can read it
items.say: Encryption, so nobody in the middle can read it.

items.title: Integrity
items.say: Integrity, so nobody can change it.

items.title: Identity
items.text: a certificate proves who it is
items.say: And a certificate, proving the site is who it claims to be.

scenes.code:
client: hello, here's what I support
server: here's my certificate
both:   agree on a key, in public
→ everything after is encrypted
scenes.say: The handshake lets both sides agree on a key, even though everyone can see the conversation.
The padlock means the connection is private. Not that the site is honest. That's HTTPS.
